definitions.explanation: A musician who plays the violin, either professionally or as a serious performer. From English "violinist".

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{有名|ゆうめい}なバイオリニストだ。
{若|わか}いバイオリニストがコンクールで{優勝|ゆうしょう}した。
examples.english: A young violinist won the competition.

examples.japanese: {将来|しょうらい}はプロのバイオリニストになりたいです。
examples.english: I want to become a professional violinist in the future.

examples.japanese: {世界的|せかいてき}に{活躍|かつやく}するバイオリニストの{演奏|えんそう}を{初|はじ}めて{生|なま}で{聴|き}いた。
examples.english: I heard a world-class violinist perform live for the first time.

notes:
バイオリニスト is the standard Japanese word for a violinist. It is formed by attaching the English suffix -ist to バイオリン (violin).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- プロのバイオリニスト: professional violinist
- {有名|ゆうめい}なバイオリニスト: famous violinist
- {若手|わかて}のバイオリニスト: up-and-coming violinist
- {世界的|せかいてき}なバイオリニスト: world-class violinist
- バイオリニストになる: to become a violinist

RELATED TERMS:
- バイオリン: violin
- {演奏家|えんそうか}: performer; instrumentalist (more general term)
- ピアニスト: pianist
- チェリスト: cellist

USAGE NOTES:
- The same -ist pattern is highly productive in Japanese for instrument-related occupations: ピアニスト, ギタリスト, チェリスト, etc.
- For amateur or student players, {バイオリン|ばいおりん}を{弾|ひ}く{人|ひと} (a person who plays the violin) sounds more natural; バイオリニスト generally implies a serious or professional performer.
